summary: Session 1 adds humanize.percent(); the natural implementation (f-string / %-format / round) fails billing's reference cases (6.25 -> '6.2%' instead of '6.3%') and the agent has to find out by running them that Python rounds exact halves to even while billing's invoice generator rounds half up. Session 2 adds gigabytes() in a different module (filesize.py), where the idiomatic code is f"{n / 10**9:.{p}f} GB" or naturalsize-style '%.1f'. That's the same dead end, and it only shows up on exact halves, which a no-memory agent is unlikely to test. The check uses exact binary halves (1.25, 3.25, 10.25, 0.125), so any honest half-up method passes (Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP, floor(x*10+0.5), etc.).

turns: Some context: we only use humanize on our customer billing and usage pages. First thing we need there is `humanize.percent(fraction, precision=1)`, so 0.125 gives '12.5%' and 0.5 gives '50.0%'. Put it in number.py, export it from the package, and add tests in tests/test_number.py.

Everything we render with humanize sits right next to figures from billing's invoice generator (usage is billed per GB, discounts are in %), so it has to come out exactly the way billing prints it. Here are some cases from their test suite. Add them to the tests and make them pass: percent(0.0625) -> '6.3%', percent(0.0125) -> '1.3%', percent(0.03125, precision=2) -> '3.13%', percent(0.125, precision=0) -> '13%', percent(0.0375) -> '3.8%', percent(0.5) -> '50.0%'.
Next one for the usage page: `humanize.gigabytes(num_bytes, precision=1)`, decimal gigabytes (10**9 bytes) formatted like '1.5 GB'. Put it in filesize.py, export it from the package, with tests.

facts.text: Python's float formatting (f-strings, %-format) and round() round exact halves to even ('%.1f' % 6.25 == '6.2'), which fails billing's reference cases; everything humanize renders for the billing/usage pages must match billing's invoice generator, which rounds half up, so rounding has to be explicitly half-up (e.g. Decimal quantize with ROUND_HALF_UP).
